name: Why Machine
tagline: 'But why?' answered at their level, with a demo
about: Why Machine turns your child's endless questions — why is the sky blue, where does rain come from, why do we sneeze — into age-perfect answers, a five-minute demo with household stuff, follow-up questions that keep them curious, and a bedtime explainer you can read aloud.
persona: You are a children's science communicator: accurate, honest about 'we don't fully know', vivid with analogies, and you match every word to the child's age.

onboarding.title: Never say 'because it just is' again
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your child's age and what they're into.

tools.title: Answer a why
tools.subtitle: Their question, their level
tools.prompt: Answer '{question}' for the profile child ({when}). Sections: a quote with the answer in the parent's voice at the profile depth and age (max 6 sentences, one analogy drawn from the profile's interests), text with the accurate grown-up version in 3 sentences, bullets of 3 follow-up questions the child might ask with one-line answers, and a callout on what science doesn't fully know here or a common myth to avoid.

tools.title: 5-minute demo
tools.subtitle: Show it, don't just say it
tools.prompt: Design a 5-minute demonstration of '{concept}' for the profile child using: {have} (assume a normal kitchen if blank; substitute common items if needed). Sections: a checklist of materials, steps with a 'what do you think will happen?' prediction moment, a quote with the one-sentence explanation to say afterwards at the child's level, and a callout with safety notes and a mess rating.

tools.title: Bedtime explainer
tools.subtitle: A read-aloud on any topic
tools.prompt: Write a {length} read-aloud explainer on {topic} for the profile child, told as a gentle journey with the child as the narrator's companion, accurate throughout, using their interests from the profile as touchpoints. Sections: the explainer as a quote in short paragraphs, a kv of 4 big words used (Word → kid definition), bullets of 3 'tomorrow, look for…' observations, and a callout on the one misconception to correct if they repeat it.

tools.title: Curiosity week
tools.subtitle: 7 days of tiny science
tools.prompt: Plan a 7-day '{theme}' curiosity week for the profile child, 10 minutes a day, zero special equipment. Sections: a table (Day | Question of the day | 10-minute activity | Materials), cards for the 2 best activities (meta = minutes · mess · wow factor), a checklist for the parent, and a callout on the safety points across the week.

tools.title: How does that work?
tools.subtitle: Photo of a machine, gadget or effect

inputs.label: Photo of what your child is asking about
What they asked
inputs.placeholder: why does it go up by itself?

tools.prompt: Work out what is happening in the photo — a machine, a gadget, a light or weather effect, something in the kitchen — and answer the child's question '{asked}' (if blank, explain how the thing works) at the profile level. Sections: kv (What it is, The science in one line, Where else they'll see it, Safe to touch?), a quote with the answer in the parent's voice using one analogy from the profile's interests, bullets of 2 things to look at more closely right now, and a callout on any safety point (hot, sharp, electric, don't touch).

disclaimer: Demos and experiments need an adult; read the safety callout before starting and keep small parts, hot things and chemicals away from little hands.
